fieldMarks: Smooth, unkeeled scales, gray to olive above (CPW).
Orange or yellow ring around the neck, usually bordered in black (CPW; NPS Jewel Cave).
Belly orange with black spots and red underside of the tail; when threatened it coils the tail to show the red underside (CPW; NPS Jewel Cave).
Small and slender: rarely over about 42 cm (16.5 in), average about 14 in (CPW; NPS Jewel Cave).
behavior: Hides by day under flat rocks, logs or other cover and is rarely seen in the open; several of mixed age may share one rock, especially in spring (CPW; NatureServe).
Eats earthworms, slugs, small salamanders, frogs, lizards and snakes (NatureServe).
Releases a foul musk when caught (NPS Jewel Cave).
Inactive in winter in most areas; eggs are often laid communally (NatureServe).
habitat: Forests, woodlands, grassland, chaparral and riparian corridors; moist at least seasonally; often near abandoned buildings and junk piles in wooded areas (NatureServe; CPW).
range: Coast to coast across North America; northern limit of the continuous range reaches Nova Scotia, southern Quebec and southern Ontario, and it occurs disjunctly in the West (NatureServe).
